niche: which of a bike-share operator's five classic networks gets 300 e-bikes and the net fare revenue a year they add, when the busiest network's stations rarely run dry and the campus network's residence-hall hubs run dry at every teaching-weekday class change, so the rides on record understate the requests
answer: University: USD 125,000 a year in net fare revenue at 2025 demand (Central USD 75,000, Riverside USD 50,000, Old Town USD 25,000, Hillcrest USD 25,000)
analyst_test: A strong analyst reads every field and rule correctly, measures the Harbour pilot's e-bike share (41.7 per cent of rides) and new-rider uplift (4.4 per cent), carries them to each network's 2025 rides at its classic fare and the e-bike premium, and names Central at about USD 50,000 a year, because no field, flag or document says a request met an empty station.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is a launch's incremental revenue against the existing product, the uplift a product analyst sizes from a pilot, and in shared mobility the existing product's usage is censored by availability: a dock that runs dry records no request, so the trips on record are served demand only.
layer1: two trip systems across the 1 July platform switch: station names against station codes, legacy against new account ids, three bike-number formats, fares in dollars against cents
local time with the repeated November hour in the trip exports; the dispatch log, charging and workshop exports in UTC
false starts (an undock put straight back) in the trip exports
the 03:00 audit as a fleet-audit workbook, GBFS station and region feeds
the City's open data by area and month with small cells suppressed
re-registered accounts, re-sent charging sessions and road-test retests in the asks' files

spine.entity: one undock (a ride or a false start)

driver: A launch's added revenue is sized from requests, but the record holds only the requests the service met: where the existing supply runs out at every peak, the unmet requests leave no row, so carrying a pilot's uplift by each candidate's recorded use sends the launch to the candidate whose supply never runs out; only the supply rebuilt second by second from the movements in and out shows which candidate turns away the most requests.
driver_concrete: Each network's turned-away requests are rebuilt from each station's classic stock (the 03:00 audit, then every undock, dock and van move, second by second) and its requests per stocked second by month, day type and hour, and University, whose residence-hall hubs run dry at every class change, adds the most net fare revenue, while Central, with the most rides on record, rarely runs dry.
stump: A competent analyst carries the pilot's e-bike share and new-rider uplift to each network's 2025 rides and names Central at about USD 50,000 a year, against University at USD 125,000, whose residence-hall hubs turn away the class-change requests the trip record never shows.

differentiation.task199: task199 reads an event rate from a record that holds an event only where a watcher filed an account, against the watchers' filing volumes; task308's record holds every met request and loses only the ones that met an empty station, and the turned-away requests are rebuilt from each station's stock, rebuilt second by second from trips, van moves and the nightly count.
differentiation.task268: task268 v2 measures how far a stock fell through collectors who sample where they find most; task308 measures how many requests an empty station turned away, from the station's own rebuilt stock and its requests in the steps it was stocked, with no sampler choosing where to look.
differentiation.task196: task196 v2 recovers events a record partly captures from the overlap of two capture channels; task308 has one channel, the trip record, and recovers the requests it never captured from the steps in which the station had no bike.
differentiation.task255: task255 v1 fits a size distribution's tail with item-specific truncation and a moving censoring ceiling; task308 counts turned-away requests at docks whose stock, not a recording threshold, censors the count, and the censoring times are rebuilt from the flows in and out.
differentiation.task271: task271 v2 reweights reached members by each state's chance of being reached in each window of the day, a nonresponse model fitted to call histories; task308 has no nonresponse and no states: each station's empty windows are rebuilt exactly from the flows in and out, and the requests in them come from the same station's requests in the windows it was stocked.
differentiation.task471: task471 v1 weights each returned reply by the share of handout days from which a trip of its length could come back, a selection on return windows; task308 weights no record: it adds the requests that left no record because the station was empty, counted from the station's own rebuilt stock.
differentiation.task305: task305 adds a body of short-stay occupants whom the demand model's resident origins never count, measured at outlets beside similar lodgings; task308's riders are all in the record's population, and what the record misses is the requests those riders made when the station had no bike, recovered from the station's own stock and request rate.
